newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB's calculation of its own finances correct - BOJ.
newsitem.headline: NCB's calculation of its own finances correct - BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that the BOJ had confirmed that Nippon Credit Bank's (NCB) calculations of its own financial conditions were correct.
Matsushita, in response to a question at a parliamentary committee meeting, said the BOJ follows up as needed on its regular inspections of financial institutions.
Such a follow-up examination was recently conducted at NCB by a BOJ expert on inspections of financial firms, he said.
Based on the expert's examination, the central bank confirmed that NCB's calculations of its financial conditions were "appropriate", Matsushita said.

NCB, a major Japanese bank, last week announced a restructuring plan under which it plans to halt overseas operations, sell off its Tokyo headquarters and post losses to dispose of problem loans. The restructuring plan was based on NCB's own calculations of its financial conditions.
"Although its total assets will decrease, the bank's liabilities will not exceed its assets. That's why the BOJ decided to take what measures it could to boost the bank's capital," Matsushita said.
